the second incorrectly reduces required work because time is unavailable and miscounts available nights.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03101","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 120/2 as 60/2 = 30, then gives an unsupported final answer of 15.","case2_error":"Calculates only Jake’s consumption, omitting his brother’s and father’s papayas from the four-week purchase.","reason":"The first contains an explicit numerical evaluation error and unsupported final number; the second omits consumers from the required total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03102","case1_error":"States correct cost formulas but supplies 475 without supporting calculation; the formulas yield 752.","case2_error":"Replaces the correctly calculated 5700 goal with funds raised plus miscellaneous expenses, producing an erroneous remaining requirement.","reason":"An unsupported number after correct formulas differs from explicitly redefining the target using an incorrect relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03103","case1_error":"Uses one Monday counting session instead of Tuesday’s two tile-counting sessions when adding Tuesday counts.","case2_error":"Treats the per-pair price as Monday’s spending, assigns 60 to Tuesday, and ignores Tuesday’s fourfold spending relation.","reason":"The first substitutes a count from the wrong day; the second confuses unit price with daily spending and fails to apply a multiplier.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03104","case1_error":"Divides Grenada’s supplies between bases, invents equal base totals, omits guns, and makes further numerical errors.","case2_error":"Adds capacities of one boxcar per color without multiplying by the numbers of boxcars.","reason":"The first invents allocation and equality relations and miscalculates; the second omits multiplicities when aggregating correctly calculated unit capacities.","judgment":"different"}]}
